thread.title: PayPal (PYPL): A bet on the boom of digital payments

author: Admin
title: PayPal (PYPL): A bet on the boom of digital payments
text:
PayPal (PYPL): A bet on the boom of digital payments February 23, 2018 tweet 
The shares of PayPal (PYPL) are generating extraordinary returns for investors: they accumulate a rise of more than 80 per cent in the last 4 quarters. 
We analyze the main factors behind these attractive gains, as well as the key price levels to watch and the risks to consider when assessing a position in the digital payments company. 
Growing at full speed 
The main driver behind PayPal’s attractive price performance in recent months has to do with the company’s vigorous growth rates, which announced both sales and profits above market expectations in the last quarter. And the main operational indicators of the business are moving in the right direction. 
PayPal’s sales during the fourth quarter of 2017 amounted to $3.7B, growing 24% year-on-year in dollars. Earnings per share of the firm amounted to $0.55 per unit, increasing 31% year-on-year. 
The total volume of payments was $114B, which represents a significant growth compared to the same quarter of the previous year. The company ended the fourth quarter of 2017 with 227 million active accounts, earning 8.7 million new active accounts in the period. 
The number of transactions per user is increasing. The data is clearly positive in terms of assessing the company’s ability to generate value for users and sustain future growth rates. 
Additionally, profit margins were expanding. Adjusted operating margin grew by 100 basis points during the quarter, reaching 21.8% ​​of the company’s sales. 
Not only did the last quarter set a record high for PayPal in terms of sales and profits, but the data also showed an acceleration in growth rates compared to previous quarters. Obviously, this is a powerful tailwind for the price of the shares. 
Valuation and key risk factors 
PayPal shares broke higher in May 2017, and prices have since maintained a well-defined uptrend. With the asset recently testing its historical price highs, the validity of this trend is out of the question. 
In case of price adjustment, the area of ​​$76.86 per share could work again as a support. To the extent that this support is respected, the price action is considered favorable upwards. 
In terms of valuation, PayPal shares are priced at fairly aggressive levels. The price-earnings ratio is ​​28 times the expected earnings for next year. In comparison, the average for companies in the S & P 500 index is a ratio-price earnings of 22.9 times the expected results. 
The digital payment company has demonstrated over time its capacity to generate levels of growth that justify a valuation above the market average. Beyond this, the current price of shares does not allow too much margin to cushion eventual bad news. Therefore, their shares could be vulnerable to the downside if the firm’s performance is not up to expectations. 
Competitive risk is another important factor to consider. Large technology companies such as Apple (AAPL), Amazon (AMZN) and Google (GOOG) are entering the digital payments business in recent years. The same goes for many of the big banks and credit and debit card operators. 
PayPal’s strategy has been to form alliances with these players, in order to limit the competitive pressure and prioritize the future growth potential over the profit margins for each transaction. Judging by the company’s financial reports, the strategy is providing the expected results, both in terms of business numbers and in terms of the company’s strategic positioning. 
On the other hand, given that it operates in a rapidly evolving industry with an ever changing ecosystem, it is important to closely monitor the competitive dynamics in the business and PayPal’s ability to adapt to new trends in the market. 
Considering the valuation of the shares, as well as the sector in which the company operates, it is clear that PayPal is an investment alternative with risk levels above the average. On the other hand, the financial performance of the business is more than promising, and the price action supports the possibility of additional price gains in the medium term. TAGS
